text.p: These are the main stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian collective presidency, with assitance of U.S. envoys Robert Gelbard and Richard Holbrooke, reached long-awaited agreement on distribution of diplomatic posts, telecommunication system and standing committee for military matters.
- Council of Ministers is due to meet on Friday after they failed to agree on citizenship law and issuing of new passports.
- Moslem authorities in Mostar and representatives of international community agreed on procedures for the return of Moslem and Croat refugees to western and eastern sectors of town.

- According to a decision by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, leading Moslem, Serb and Croat national parties will not qualify for financial assistance for their pre-electoral campaigns, as part of an effort to create a balance among all political parties running for municipal elections.
- Workers from coal mines in Zenica, Bila, Breza and Kakanj ended their strike following a letter allowing payment of June salaries for about 5,000 miners.

- Washington has decided to drive the Bosnian car at maximum speed, says newspaper commentary. U.S. envoys shortened some deadlines that Izetbegovic and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman had agreed on, making it clear to them that action on key peace agreement provisions had to start immediately.

- Opposition Social Democratic Party deputy, Zlatko Lagumdzija, urged the establishment of a parliamentary commission for collecting data on prisoners and conditions in prisons. --Sarajevo newsroom +387 71 663 384
